correctness.rationale: For each admissible index set \(I\), Wang's term is \(\theta_I=S_I/P+(|I|-3)/q_I\), where \(P\) is the product of all weights and \(q_I\) is the product of the omitted weights. The full set gives \(S/P+n-2\). For every proper set, \(S_I<S\), \(q_I\ge1\), and \(|I|\le n\), so \((|I|-3)/q_I\le n-3<n-2\); hence every proper term is strictly smaller. Substitution into Proposition 3.17 yields the global hyperbolicity criterion. The full set is indeed included in Wang's maximum, as is also forced by the dimension-three case and Corollary 3.18.

value.rationale: The quantity \(\Theta\) is the natural controlling invariant in Wang's global theorem. Computing it exactly removes an exponential-looking optimization over toric strata and shows structurally that boundary recursion costs no additional degree. This materially sharpens the paper's general corollary: for example, \(\mathbf P(1,1,2,3,5)\) is globally covered already at \(m=3\), whereas the printed coarse weighted bound gives a much larger threshold. The result is therefore a reusable closed-form theorem about the source's main parameter rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
